translations.text: in the desert, in my father's house, to repent of my many wicked deeds.
And this is what is in my heart: even if I will not be worthy to see the Lord face to face, openly, in the place where I am going, because I am a sinful man,
still I will strive to be filled with him secretly here on earth, since he bars no one, neither me nor anyone who repents,
or who will repent. And if I go to him, he is sufficient in his compassion to have mercy on me in my poverty.
This alone is how I pray in my house, confessing my sins before the Lord,
saying through my tears, “May I be worthy to see him in the place where I am going, and let him punish me with fire.”
But I believe that he will have mercy on me through your prayers, brothers.
And I think that those who strive to be filled with him on earth through prayers, fasts, nights of keeping watch, and praises,
and much meditation and learning, in complete submission and humility, with complete obedience and wisdom, and all the other deeds,
are also the ones who will be filled with him in the place where they are going. And they are the ones who will see him face to face in that place.
But those who are always disobedient, who hate God, who are proud, boastful, undisciplined, hardhearted, slow to understand, insolent, ungrateful, filthy,
and defiled in their conscience, which burns against them with strife, hatred, and hostility, with contempt and rejection of the word of God,
with grumbling, faultfinding, boasting, sexual immorality, and all the many other things, and every evil deed—
those who do these things and the others will never be worthy to be filled with the Lord Jesus through faith here on earth,
much less to see him face to face in heaven, in the place where they are going. Indeed, it is people like these whom he will burn with a fire that is never extinguished.
I said these things to you to let you know that I wanted to remain in my house, repenting all the days of my life.
But now, in turn, I tell you that I want to remain among my brothers, the children of God,
and the children of my fathers, so that we may benefit one another. For this is God's will, and this is the will of my fathers. I have been living in the desert for more than a hundred years,
and this is how I wish to bear everything that comes upon me, as though I were doing nothing.
The old man and all the elders are the ones who toil at every task. And we thank the brothers who labor with us, those who obey our word in everything they are able to do,
and those who give our hearts relief through complete submission, working for their salvation with fear and trembling.
We know who they all are, from the least to the greatest.
Therefore God will bless them,
and he will protect them from every evil thing, and he will give them rest in every way in heaven, in the place where they are going.
But those who are disobedient in everything, who reject the word of the Lord through their disobedience and their reliance on themselves alone—we know who they are.

For this reason the Lord will forgive them, because they are our brothers and fellow members of the body, and because they too are weak in their ignorance. We ourselves are grieved over them because they have not also served us in providing for our bodily comfort.
We thank those who offer us their evening portion, or indeed anything of theirs, out of love.
And it is the Lord who will repay them according to their good deeds.
Nor are we grieved because those people have spoken against us, for we deserve it.
For this reason, as things stand, they do us no harm by speaking against us, or by grumbling among themselves off to one side, or by finding fault with our way of life.

If only the Lord would also grant us the ability to turn our cheek to the one who strikes it, and, if we too should be killed for the name of our God, to say willingly, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
But we are distressed and grieve day and night
over those who disobey the gospel of our Lord Jesus, who says, “Unless you turn and become like these little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.”
See now how clearly the ignorance of those among us who are wise in their own eyes has been revealed, whether male or female, great or small.
I say these things, brothers, so that no one among us, whether here with us or there with you, may lose heart while bearing with those around them.
For it is the Lord who will give you your reward. Therefore do not be distressed if they mock you or ridicule you and speak evil words against you.
It is no wonder if those people insult you, spit in your face, or strike you on the head,
like the messenger of Satan, as it is written: “We are hungry, we are thirsty, we are naked, we are beaten, we are troubled, we toil.
When they persecute us, we endure them; when they slander us, we appeal to them.”
Rather, what is remarkable is that they should not be made to stumble through you by any evil deed, as it is written.
We are not shaming you by telling you these things,
but are instructing you as a beloved brother, so that we may not be condemned along with the world, and so that we may escape the words of our prophet: “Look,
I will bring disasters upon this people and upon the fruit of their disobedience, because they have not paid attention to my word; they have abandoned my law.”
For this reason I beg you, brothers, to keep yourselves away from every fight and every quarrel, every evil deed and every bodily desire—

these things that wage war against your souls—so that we may circumcise the uncircumcision of our hard hearts, and so that the Lord may make you grow in every good work, to do his will for him, as he works in us what is pleasing before him.
For this is the will of God: your purification, so that we may be holy to him and love one another as he commanded us according to the Scriptures.
What is circumcision of the heart, or what is uncircumcision?
Those who live at all times in hardness of heart, stubbornness, slowness to understand, and unwillingness to learn,

and in disobedience, obstinacy, fighting, quarreling, jealousy, hatred, defilement, and every evil deed—these are the ones who are uncircumcised in their hearts and also in their ears, according to the Scriptures.
But those who live at all times in humility, gentleness, patience, love, and willingness to learn, with complete submission, complete obedience, and every kind of goodness,
[?] man or woman among you who pours water over their head to wash their face, out of a desire to leave themselves [?] of the hair on their head, in vanity and a passion for pleasure.
Cursed is any man or woman among you who washes their feet improperly, out of desire,
or secretly wets themselves with water, or secretly anoints themselves with oil, without first consulting the elder among us or the elder woman among you.
Cursed is any man or woman among you who sets their heart on a garment, a tunic, a covering, or a hood,
or sandals, wanting them to be made nicely for themselves, saying, “They are ours,” rather than having one common standard for everyone, from the greatest to the least.
Cursed is any man or woman among you who favors their relatives by birth, whom they have had admitted, over strangers
and orphans among you, whether in food, clothing, any other supplies, or any other matter.
Cursed is any man or woman among you who secretly eats anything beyond the allowance laid down for us,
whether a piece of fish, cooked fish, salted fish, an egg, cheese, [?], milk, or any other supplies beyond the allowance.
Therefore, do not let anyone deceive us, either here among us or there among you, into touching or tasting any of these things at all.
Do not even let us think about them at all.
Nor let us desire them so as to keep them for ourselves, just as our fathers guarded themselves against these things.
They too were once sick and endured very great suffering. But because of you, so that we should not die,
they did not touch or taste any of [?].
They will defile themselves in any way, whether they are away from home or in the congregation.
And anyone among you who sins or will sin secretly, here among us or there among you, and does not confess the sin they have committed—these curses will come upon them,
all of them. And also those who offer the offering anywhere else in our district in rivalry, whether they are in fellowship with us or instead live near us without being in fellowship with us,
and anyone who offers the offering anywhere else in our district in rivalry, rather than within our congregations, where all the brothers are gathered.
and down at our father's sanctuary, where the church is in the desert—they will be cursed.
Our district extends from the canal north of the village of Triphiou southward to the canal south of the house of our aged father Apa Psoi, the place where he first lived in the desert.
Everyone who settles near us will be bound by the rules laid down for all the brothers who gather together
for four weeks of the year, which our father established for us.
Everyone living in the desert of our district must also assemble with the brothers, so that they come together, unless prevented by illness.
But anyone living in the desert who is unwilling to live according to the regulations our fathers laid down for us—
if they are in our congregations, we will expel them from them, whether they are a man or a woman.
And if they are in the desert of our district, we will assemble and go to the place where they are and drive them away from our neighborhood.
But if he defiantly rebels against us, we will tear down the place where he lives and forcibly throw him out of there.
But we will be careful not to strike him, lest we give occasion for a death.
And we will tear down the place where he was living and demolish it to its foundations, so that no one will ever live in it and cause his neighbor to stumble.
And those among us who at any time flee from the elder and go to bishops without permission, to have hands laid on them in defiance,
will be cursed, because obedience is better than their presenting offerings in disobedience and lack of discipline.

But as for anyone who lives according to the rules laid down for us, no one may spitefully expel him, whether he is in the desert around us or in the congregation with us, here with us or there with you.
But if a time comes when sin overpowers those living in this place at that time, because of the hardness of heart that will come upon everyone who transgresses the commandments laid down for them,
here in this desert where we now are,
then at that time anyone who wishes to flee into the desert, anywhere, to save himself is free from all these curses,

to live on this mountain and also to present an offering wherever he wishes, in the fear of God, taking care not to offer a sacrifice anywhere except the place that the Lord God has chosen for himself, according to the Scriptures.
And those who come to us to live with us, whether male or female, or those in the desert around us—everyone who shares in our fellowship among us, here with us or there with you—
and they do not renounce all the possessions they have, whether gold, silver, or copper,
whether clothing or any possessions, will be cursed, because they have not taken up their cross to follow the Lord.
And anyone who sets his heart on any of the possessions that he renounced in order to come under the bond of God's community and the service of the poor,
so that he turns back, denies his commitment, and looks for a way to take them back again, will be cursed, having become like Ananias and his wife Sapphira,
and like Cain and the others with whom the Lord has not been pleased, from the beginning until now.
And whoever gives things away secretly to the elder and the brothers will be cursed before God.
And anyone who secretly takes oil, money, clothing, or anything else and gives it to his relatives outside, or to anyone else outside, will be cursed before the Lord.
And anyone among us, here with us or there with you, who secretly and deceitfully gives things to his neighbor, whether food,
clothing, shoes, a belt, or absolutely any other article, in secret,

without first informing the elder here with us, or without first informing the woman elder there with you, will be cursed, because they have transgressed the commandments that our fathers entrusted to us:
that no one, whether male or female, should secretly and deceitfully give anything to his neighbor,
without its being authorized by the elder here with us, or by the woman elder appointed for you there with you.

And anyone who shaves himself, or those who shave another person among us, whether male or female, without authorization, will be cursed, because they have transgressed the commandments that our fathers entrusted to us.

And whoever removes a thorn from the foot of someone among us, whether man or woman, without necessity and without authorization, will be cursed, because they have dishonored the commandments that our fathers entrusted to us.
But a case of necessity is when we are away from home or traveling on a road, far from the congregation, or alternatively,
when we are in the congregation and a thorn troubles someone's foot or hand, and because of the urgency of the pain, the person near him is to pull it out for him in the fear of God.

And this is how it is to be for someone away from home, someone traveling on the road with his neighbor, or any other brother: the person near him is to pull it out for him with great fear and trembling.
Whoever harbors filthy thoughts in his heart, or tolerates a foul desire in his spirit while being fondled, or himself fondles the person beside him, or
has his foot tickled, or himself tickles the feet of the person beside him, will be cursed, whether male or female.
Again, those who sleep two together on one mat, or who sleep close enough together to touch or press against one another at all with lustful passion, will be cursed, whether male or female.
Again, those who remain seated close to the person beside them with a foul desire in their hearts will be cursed, whether male or female.

Again, those who get up from their sleeping places and approach the sleeping places of those beside them to fondle them with lustful passion while they are asleep and unaware, or else while they are aware and tolerate one another, speaking with [?]

urine into a bottle or into a pot, or into any other similar vessel, without authorization from the elder, except only in the place for the sick and the elderly who have advanced in years. The others are to ask the elder.
And if a need arises for some among us to use something like this, to urinate into any vessel of this kind because of the necessity caused by a wound,
or a sore [?] on someone's foot that makes him unable to walk outside, they are to ask the elder.
Apart from these, if young children or anyone else urinates into any vessel of this kind, they will be cursed.
Cursed is anyone who slanderously attributes a sinful act to the person beside him,
without knowing for certain, but out of hatred says something that is not true, whether male or female.
Cursed is anyone who deceitfully says, “I saw a dream in which so-and-so and so-and-so were defiling themselves with every kind of evil deed,” whether male or female.
Cursed are all those who practice deceit in any of the Lord's congregations,
causing God to become angry with a great multitude and turn his face away from them in wrath because of the wickedness of those who commit lawlessness among us, secretly or openly.
And woe to those through whom God will be troubled and seek a way to leave their midst,

like a righteous person who seeks a way to abandon a people because of their evil deeds, according to the prophet's words: “Who will give me a distant dwelling place in the wilderness, so that I may abandon this people and go far away from them?”
But blessed are all those through whom God will be reassured, so that he is willing to remain among them,
like a righteous person who has been reassured by faithful people and has been willing to remain among them at all times.
For the Lord himself is also among them at all times because of their true and righteous deeds.
But anyone among us who witnesses a deceitful act involving impurity,
or theft, or any other sin that leads to death, and does not tell me who it is or what those evil deeds are—
all these curses will come upon them from God, whether male or female.
As for all the others who ought to be cursed in this letter but whom we have not cursed, look: they are all recorded in the documents written previously.
As for the holy words of our Lord Jesus that are written in the Scriptures and in this letter, I will tell you what they resemble.
They resemble lamps that have been lit in dark places.
And they are like daylight.
And the senseless, who go to great extremes in foolishness, are like bats.
And just as bats—that is, the creatures called chinchlo—plunge downward or flee into the darkness or into cramped places,
whenever they see the light of the flame of lamps and the daylight,
so too the senseless and those who go to great extremes in foolishness will plunge downward or into their passions and desires,
and into the darkness of their false knowledge, when confronted with all the words of our Lord, whether those from the Scriptures
or those from this letter—not these alone, but also all the others written in these sheets that have been written from the beginning.
Again, the holy words of our Lord Jesus are like the light of lamps in the hands of a wise person,
lighting his way in dark places as he does his work,
as it is written: “Your word is a lamp for my feet.”
And they are like daylight.
And whoever pays attention to them will not stumble, according to the Scriptures: “Whoever walks in the daytime does not stumble.”
Therefore, blessed are the children of light, who are those who walk confidently in complete submission, complete obedience, and every good deed.
But woe to the children of darkness, who are those who walk in every kind of disobedience and lack of discipline,
fleeing into the darkness of every evil deed, like bats fleeing into very cramped, dark places.
Why did the Lord God say through his saints, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him, and if he is thirsty, give him something to drink”?
Why, on the other hand, did he say, “If your brother does not listen to you, let him be to you like a Gentile and a tax collector”?
When he says, “Do every kind of good for your enemies,” in accordance with the commandment,
he wants the good person who belongs to God to perfect his goodness through the wickedness of the evil person who belongs to the sinner, Satan.
For where the evil person shows wickedness, the good person's goodness removes the wickedness of that hostile person.
When a person repays evil with good, he fully expresses God's divinity.
But when a person repays good with evil, he fully expresses the godlessness of the godless devil.
But when he says, “If your brother does not listen to you, let him be an enemy to you, like someone you have never seen,”
first, the Lord wants us to cut him off from us after we have rebuked him, so that perhaps he may come to his senses after becoming like a stranger for God's sake, although he is our brother,
and turn back and repent, and we may forgive him seventy times seven times, provided he does not repeat the sin because of which we intended to cut him off from us.
But if he is unwilling to turn away from the sin for which we intended to cut him off from us, we will cut him off from us, and he must not return to us, nor must we love him.
Instead, he will be an enemy to us for God's sake, even though he is our brother.
In this way, the person who loves God shows the Lord his wholehearted devotion: he has loved him more than his brother, and more than his father and mother.
For it is a great degree of perfection for a person to cut off from himself his brother or his son or his daughter or his father or his mother or anyone else belonging to him, for God's sake,
whenever they sin against the one who created them, who is God.

And it is a great act of strength for a person to love his enemies for God's sake, and to pray for those who pursue him to do him harm, and, for God's sake, to bless those who curse him, sinning against him.
And this is how he said it: "Let your brother be to you like a pagan and a tax collector," for God's sake, whenever he sins before the Lord.
But as for your enemy who sins against you, love him and bless him for God's sake.
As for us, brothers, insofar as we share fellowship with one another, we are children of one person, who is God.
And we are children of one mother, who is the heavenly Jerusalem, according to the Scriptures.
Are our father and mother, then, who gave birth to us and raised us physically, preferable to our Lord Jesus, our true father and mother,
who gave birth to us through his holy blood?
[?] very great suffering [?]
with every suffering weighing upon me.
As for the young girls about whom we have heard
that they run to one another with sexual desire,
give me reliable information about them so that I may know,
and I will tell you what you are to do with them.
And again, concerning this woman about whom you said
that she should go to the place you assigned her
to do her work there, after she had told you,
"If you take me out of this place to that one,
I will not do the work I am doing."
And if she really has refused,
then tell me again, and I will instruct you about what you are to do with her.
But all of you, if you hide some deceitful matter among you from us by not telling us about it,
you are stirring up Satan against your own selves,
and you yourselves are turning God's help away from you.
Look, I have sent the old man to you this time too, as long as we are alive.
The way they behave is like animals without understanding.
But the Lord is compassionate and merciful, showing mercy.
And all those who have come to him believing in him—have they ever called on his name?
And what good have they ever done for his name in his presence?
And yet they are ignorant;
They have not loved the Lord's will.
Therefore, perhaps the words that are written will be fulfilled concerning them:
that they should receive light punishments from the Lord as servants who do not know, and the [?] will see that they are blind.
But you who sin, or who will sin deliberately among us—the Lord curses you, saying, “If you were blind, you would have no sin.
But now you say, ‘We can see.’ Your sin remains upon you.”
Therefore [?] leave you like a [?] with no water in it,
and like a garden and a vineyard whose owners have abandoned them, no longer watching over them at all,
because there is no fruit on their trees, no grapes on their vines, and no figs on their fig trees.
Even their leaves have withered, according to the Scriptures.
And so they have become plunder, for foreigners to plunder them [?].
This is also what will happen to you: God's angels will abandon you and no longer watch over you at all,
because there is no reflection, no fear of God, and no truth within you.
You would never have sinned deliberately.
But the fear of the Lord is not before your eyes to keep you from taking part in the fruitless works of darkness.
And so you have become plunder.
to him, in his holy assemblies,
so that you may share in the life of the angels.
May you bear abundant fruit, as it is written,
so that the Lord God may bless you, because you yourselves have blessed him without deceit, just as the holy angels bless him,
and so that he himself, in turn, may powerfully pour out all his blessing upon them.
May the Lord bless you so that you may be holy and be saved from every evil deed.
And may he himself give you glory, just as he gave glory to his angels,
because you yourselves have glorified him through your good deeds in the purity of your body, just as all his angels have also glorified him.
May the Lord bless you and give you glory through himself, through all his angels and all the holy companies, and through everyone who comes to you,
just as you are called angels, although you are human beings.
But you follow the way of life of God's angels and make yourselves like the prophets and the apostles
and all the saints—not merely through your outward appearance and an empty name,
like the many who take on the outward form of devotion to God
but deny its power, but through all the sufferings you endure for the name of the Lord Christ Jesus,
and so that you may be worthy of the promises he made to his prophets, his apostles, and all his saints.
Therefore the Lord will bless [?]
Therefore, then, no being will survive under his sins if he does not repent.
What is repentance except for us to withdraw from every deceit and every disobedience, the root of every evil deed?
These things and everything like them—those who read them and those who hear them, or those who teach others from them,
while they themselves transgress them all—these people
of this kind, whether they are men,
or whether they are women, expose themselves
and curse their own souls.
Therefore, cursed is everyone who reads in all the Scriptures of the Lord
while committing acts of sexual immorality, impurity, defilement, theft, deceit, and false oaths,
and does not repent of the uncleanness and defilement they have committed.
But even more cursed is everyone who reaches out their hands toward the holy Gospels of our Lord Jesus
and open them with their hands, which are full of every kind of filth and impurity,
to read in them while living in much deceit, envy, hatred, inhumanity, and every especially evil deed, along with many sins
that lead to death, as it is written:
“There is sin that leads to death.”
And there is no way to plead with God on behalf of those who commit them, so that he may forgive them
completely, because it is not one brother, nor two,
who have done what is especially evil in the Lord’s sight.
For this reason I tell you, brothers,
that all who read the books of the Lord
and study the words of the Scriptures of God,
but do not heal themselves through their own deeds,
are brothers of the one who destroys himself, as it is written:
“How does a person destroy himself,
unless he brings an abomination into his house,
so that he becomes an abomination in God’s sight, suffering great destruction?”
What is our house but our congregation
and we ourselves? And what is the abomination that we will bring into our house but sexual immorality, defilement, theft, falsehood, and every evil deed?
Who is the brother of the one who destroys himself,
if not the person who does these things and many others,
along with the person who has established for himself two different measures and a fraudulent grain measure?
Who is the one who destroys himself but the evil demon, Satan, the son of destruction,
the enemy of everyone who loves our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God?
I tell you that just as two different measures are an abomination to the Lord,
and a fraudulent grain measure is not true in his sight,
so too the person who is double-minded in his perseverance is an abomination to God.
And a deceitful person is not good in God's sight.
And no one is more accursed than someone who pleads with God
while disobeying his law.
For this reason, if they stretch out their hands to him, he will turn his face away from them.
And if they multiply their pleas, he will not listen to them, according to the Scriptures.
But consider: if we are the ones whom people sin against,
and they also pray to us as they do to God,
if we were to put up with those who plead with us while throwing dirt in our faces,
would we not be very angry?
And how will God not be angry with us when we pray to him
while also provoking him with all our evil deeds?
But we will say that many of the saints put up with those who insulted them and threw dirt in their faces,
and although many of them were killed, they blessed their killers and cried out to God
not to hold against them the sins they had committed against them.
But consider also
For God has said how severely vengeance is to be taken on them,
and how heavily the blood of those they killed will fall upon them,
just as righteous Solomon took vengeance on that man
who threw dirt in his father's face.
And just as our Lord Jesus said that all the righteous blood shed on the earth,
from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, would fall upon those murderers.
For this reason I tell you that, just as all the saints were patient with those who pursued them,
putting up with them,
leaving room for wrath on the day of wrath, as it is written,
and just as that man threw dirt in the face of our father David,
and David was patient with him.
until the day when he handed him over to his Son
to punish him with a just judgment, because he had not repented.
This is also how God is patient with those who sin,
or who will sin before him, until the end of the ages.
And on the day when he punishes us with severe punishments in the blazing furnace of fire through his holy Son Jesus,
to whom his Father gave authority to carry out judgment,
as it is written, “The Father will not judge anyone,
but he has entrusted all judgment to the Son.”
Now, brothers, let us not allow our hearts to get the better of us through foolishness, like disobedient little children from whom the rod and instruction are far removed, as it is written.
But just as a father disciplines his son with a rod,
wanting to save his soul from death because he loves him very much,
so let us also discipline ourselves through fear of standing before the Lord’s judgment seat.
And let us instruct ourselves earnestly by remembering the punishments,
knowing that we cannot endure the blazing furnace of fire, hunger, thirst, and many other afflictions.
See: everyone who learns a trade,
Unless they are disciplined, they do not carry out their work properly,
whether those in schools, carpenters, blacksmiths, or those in all the other trades.
For this reason, first of all, blessed is the Lord, because he instructs us through hardships and scourges, as it is written,
wanting us to know him rightly, as it is written:
“For the Lord disciplines the one he loves,
and he scourges every son he accepts.”
Let us, for our part, instruct ourselves in the fear of the Lord,
so that we may learn to love one another
and walk in peace and harmony.
After this, let us discipline the little boys and little girls among us with a rod,
so that they may learn to fear God
and keep his commandments, so that they may receive abundant blessing as wise people, according to the Scriptures.
For congregations that take in little children who are [?] within them are preparing wrath and anger from God for themselves—
namely, those entrusted with them, because they did not teach them to keep themselves from every impurity and every evil deed.
Therefore, teach the little girls among you
to keep their bodies from every defilement,
and to control their tongues, so that they do not indulge in joking, laughter, loose behavior, and excessive talk in idleness.
As for grown women among you, or little girls who have grown up,
who disobey those who instruct them according to the commandment
and set themselves against their parents among you, send us word about them.
And I am the one who will deal with them, so that I may oppose the disobedience and arrogance
that Satan sows within them, as it is written:
“We are ready to punish every disobedience
and every lofty thing that rises up against the knowledge of God.”
And if you do not send us word about them,
know that you are sinning against the one who created you.
There is a godliness in people's eyes that is godlessness in God's eyes, namely this:
people covering up one another's sins,
with none of them instructing another,
and none of them rebuking those around him,
so that he himself will not be rebuked in return. They say, “It is godliness,” although it is godlessness.
For they tolerate the transgressor in all his evil deeds
because he has humbled himself before them so that they will leave him to the evil desires of his heart.
They say, “God is patient,
and he does not become angry with those who sin,”
bringing destruction down upon themselves together with them, all at once, like those upon whom God brought a flood of abundant water,
because he was exceedingly angry with them in his great wrath.
And like all the others whom he has swept away from his presence from the beginning until today because they sinned against him.
And like all those whom he will curse in great anger, sending them down into the fiery furnace that burns at the end of the age,
because they did not keep his commandments.
For God is not unjust when he brings, or will bring, his wrath, with anger and a curse, upon everyone at any time who sins or will sin against him.
May that never be!
Rather, we deserve what we receive because of our evil deeds.
Therefore, according to the Scriptures, cursed is anyone who sleeps with any animal,
or indeed with any living creature at all.
Cursed is anyone who touches his neighbor’s hand,
or his foot, or indeed any part of his body, with lustful passion.
Cursed is anyone who stares into his neighbor’s face with lust.
Cursed is anyone who stretches himself out on his belly on the ground,
to make obscene movements amid thoughts of sexual immorality that torment him through the pleasure of filthy desire.
Cursed is anyone who runs up to his neighbor among us, or among you yourselves, so that he may cast glances at him

Indeed, snakes, reptiles, all wild animals, and irrational livestock love one another, each according to its own kind. But it is not for God’s sake, nor for the sake of escaping punishment,
nor for the sake of entering a place of rest.
Therefore, brothers and sisters, let us not love one another merely with words and with the tongue, as those who left us loved us with words and with the tongue.
Instead, let us love one another in deed and in truth, ready to die and to live together, like all those whose words we read—the prophets and all the saints.

Again, let us not cover up one another’s sins and make God angry with us, as many congregations covered up one another’s sins and became estranged from God without realizing it, because they did not give up earthly deeds.
Indeed, a small handful of people who keep the Lord’s commandments and are honored before him, like Noah and his household,
is better than a great crowd that transgresses before the Lord and is despised before him, like all those whom he drowned in the great waters of the flood in anger and wrath.
Again, let us not ignore what is happening among us, lest God become angry with us.
Nor let them deceive us through our circumstances, in unbelief, into trusting anything else to save us, except God alone.
Nor let them deceive us with morsels of food, varying them so that we grumble over bodily food.
Again, let us not fall into the sickness of demons and lie down in defilement and adultery,
so that our God becomes angry with us and hands us over to a perverse heart, filled with every kind of fault-finding, to judge rashly because of our insatiability and our ingratitude.
Nor let us say, as we torment one another, “You are nothing,” because God has not become angry with us in our ignorance. For who can understand what is inside a person?
It is the Lord who knows what is hidden.
He himself will also judge what happens through falsehood and what happens through the activities of demons.
And he will judge everyone who despises those who live with us or with you yourselves.
Do not let these people give anything that we do not need, lest the Lord condemn us as people who accept bribes,
and we become hateful in his sight.
Nor should we forget what is required of us according to the rules that our fathers established for us, according to the capacity and condition of our bodies, lest we become
people who despise one another before the Lord, and the Lord despise us in his presence and in the presence of his angel.
Nor should we favor ourselves over anyone through partiality, whether among us or among you yourselves,
whether we are sick or at ease, lest the Lord deal with us according to what is in our hearts
and condemn us as someone who violates the rights of the orphan, the widow, and strangers, for there is no partiality with him.
Therefore, do not let Satan cunningly deceive us into having some among us love their sons
and their daughters, or their brothers, or their parents, or any other relatives of ours more than the orphans and strangers who have no one here among us,
lest the Lord count us as strangers before him and as enemies in his presence.

And whoever neglects them in favor of his own relatives, whether among us or among you yourselves, in any matter—from a small drink of water to the smallest, most worthless vegetable, whether fruit from trees or fresh greens,
but especially oil, wine, or cooked food, and even a bed, a mat, bedding, and a lamp during their illness—and whoever favors relatives
of his own over strangers and orphans, showing partiality in these things we have mentioned and in everything like them, will be cursed before God and people.
Therefore, let us not be deceived in matters of this kind into discriminating against strangers and orphans in favor of our own relatives, showing partiality in anything.
to care for them, serve them, or stay beside them in their illness without being asked, so that the one who created us may not become angry with us
and pour out his curse upon us, just as he cursed many peoples because of deeds of this kind,

I say these things so that no one among us here or among you yourselves may sin before the Lord through these very wicked deeds, namely, favoritism:
preferring our own relatives to strangers and orphans who have no one among us.
Therefore, do not favor one person over another among you in any matter or with any goods, so that God may not become angry with you.
Instead, care for one another with fear and trembling, so that the Lord may bless you and make you grow in every good work.

What, then, is favoritism? If anyone here with us or among you yourselves gives anyone among us anything extra, beyond what has been allotted to them, without informing me first, they are sinning before the Lord.
And this is favoritism.
But if I give something to someone, whether an old man, an elderly woman, a little boy, or a little girl,
whether they are your relatives, strangers, or orphans who have no one among us,
and I instruct you to give them something extra, whether a garment, a mat for each, a sheepskin, something to eat, or anything at all,
and I give these things to them with my own hands, or tell the elder to give them to them,
or, in your own case, if we send them to you and you give them to them, no one will find anything to say against me.
Nor will there be any cause for stumbling or any sinful deed among us here or among you yourselves.
Therefore, do not go beyond us in anything,

If it is really I, or if it is the elder, who commits this great abomination in the Lord’s congregations, while you secretly slander us, saying, “They look after no one except those who have someone,”
or saying, “Indeed, they do not look after anyone fairly,” then you are more contemptuous than we are.
For sometimes you call us blessed, but at other times you abuse us terribly in secret, off by yourselves.
And those among you whom we have dismissed in distress have not told us how we wronged them or how we treated them with contempt,
so that we too might do penance for our sin, for we are miserable and poor before the Lord. For this is not in our hearts at all, not at all:
that we should forcibly lord it over a little boy or a little girl among us, much less a grown man or a grown woman,
as though we were using them by force of authority. God forbid!
Rather, this alone presses upon our hearts: to serve one another according to the apostle’s command, “Serve one another in compassionate love.”
And this is why we do not want to afflict anyone or distress anyone, whether among us or among you yourselves,
except those who anger God through their disobedience and unwillingness to learn, opposing the Lord’s law and his commandments in order to fulfill their evil desires through wicked deeds.
People of this kind will not be spared, even if others grieve and sigh because of them.
Nor will they see the joy of God while others are grieving in great distress because of them.
And just as a righteous person who keeps the Lord’s law cannot receive comfort from sinful people who break the Lord’s law,
neither can those who break the law receive comfort from a righteous person who keeps the laws.
In the same way, none of us can ever cause God and his Christ, Jesus,
and his angels and all his saints to be comforted about us if we transgress the words of the Scriptures and all his commandments.
Nor can we ourselves ever receive comfort from God if we continually persist in our sins,
while God and his Christ, Jesus, and his angels and all those who belong to him are grieving over us.
But if some among us rejoice falsely while living in their wickedness, while the Lord Jesus and his angels grieve over them as they remain in their transgressions,
then these truly are the flourishing sinners, concealing their violence and their wickedness.
Therefore, do not let some among us be deceived into rejoicing falsely in their wickedness,
as they listen to words written in places that are not counted among the canonical Scriptures of the catholic Church.
Rather, these exist to be read in this way from time to time, so that people may examine what is beneficial in them and put it into practice.
But they should leave aside the other things that are not beneficial, as people say.
Therefore, do not let some among us be deceived into rejoicing falsely in their sins as they listen to words written in certain places that say,
“Sorrow [?] within you, so that you grieve completely.”
Therefore, we are not compelled to read them; it is only our own choice that leads us to read them
and to listen to them from time to time.
Instead, we are under a far greater and most urgent obligation to read all the laws, the prophets, the apostles, and the writings of all the saints.
And we are obliged to meditate on them day and night, at all times, at every hour, and every single day,
because the entire perfection of godliness is fully realized in them.
Therefore, we ought to read and meditate at every hour and at all times on the words of the canonical Scriptures of the catholic Church,
so that we may understand how the eyes of the prophets and apostles grew dim with tears, and so that we may come to our senses and repent of our sins.
As for the additional books, which are not counted among the Scriptures, we are not to memorize them in order to meditate on them at every hour, but to read them from time to time if we wish.
But we must not read apocryphal books at all, just as those who examined what is beneficial commanded us.
Therefore, it is not only that one ought not to read hidden books at all,
But again, what are books that others have written as instruction?
And they contain sayings taken from hidden books and attached to books of letters as [?].
These other writings, too, should not be read at all by those who have been educated in the holy Scriptures.
For this reason, the Scriptures of the universal church are sufficient for us to read and learn what benefits us.
And the books of our father Athanasius, the holy archbishop, are also sufficient for us to read at all times.
And sufficient for us to read are also the books of all the others who resemble our father Athanasius, the man of God—those
whose written words were all tested beforehand [?] truly in the light of the Scriptures, so that we might be saved through their sound teaching.
Nevertheless, I too know that we should rejoice in the Lord at all times, as it is written.
But I also know that worldly sorrow produces death, according to the Scriptures.
But let us not allow the hostile, evil demons to deceive us through trickery
and let us rejoice falsely [?] God is angry with us
and pour out his wrath upon us because we rejoiced while he was grieved.
For this reason, let us repent
and weep over our sins with sorrow, sighing, and great anguish of heart, knowing
that sorrow according to God produces in us repentance without regret, for the salvation of our souls and our bodies.
Otherwise, where is it written in the writings of the prophets and the apostles that they say,
“Do not let sorrow find a place within you, and do not grieve at all”?
How, then, could our holy fathers say, “Do not grieve,”
when they themselves mixed what they were going to drink with tears, according to the Scriptures, just as they also say,
“Our eyes have poured out streams of water”?
And again, “My eyes have been troubled by weeping.”
And again, “My life has wasted away in sorrow,
and my years in sighing.”
And again, “I walked like [?] one who mourns and is downcast.” And he said,
“This was how I humbled myself.” And in many other places in the Scriptures they teach us in this way,
that this is how they grieved.
And they grieved very, very deeply, since [?] our [?] and the ancients.

that our Lord Jesus himself, too, began to grieve and be troubled in his heart, trembling intensely.
And this is what he said:
“My soul is grieved to the point of death.”

or even now, the reading of all the words written in that book, or those written in this letter and the others we have written,
or those we will write from this day onward—and those who prevent them from being read at that time
or even now—all these curses will come upon them.
But everyone, at any time, who makes an effort to have them read,
But those who are willing to listen to them, keep them, and do them—all these blessings will come upon them. For this reason, I will not only instruct the brothers
who are of one heart with us to take care of all the words that we will write in that book, together with those written in all the letters,
but I will also instruct them to preserve my clothes, which I have torn many times, finally tearing them into two pieces, as I was deeply distressed in my heart, to the point of death.
For this reason, I will instruct the brothers who are of one heart with us, those who are alive at the time of my death, to lay my torn clothes before those who come after us.
And everyone who hears, at that time or even now, all the words written in that book, or those written in the letters we have written or those we will write,
and says, “What are these torn clothes, all these written words, and all these curses?”
And they will answer and say, “Because the one who watches over the whole earth,
and who passes secretly through the whole inhabited world many times, at every moment and day after day—that is, God—
once looked down upon us too in secret and passed through our assemblies many times, without appearing to any human being, male or female, but only to his angels.
And they will say, “At that time the Lord was intensely angry with us, with great wrath.
And he turned his face away from us in great anger, to bring upon us great curses, terrible afflictions, and severe trials, because we had sinned against him,
when Satan came upon us like a ravenous, roaring lion and struck those in our care.”
And they will also say, “When we repented in deep humility, with hunger, thirst, and weeping, with tears free of hypocrisy, God turned his face away from us
and turned back his anger, so that he would not punish us with great and terrible trials.
And he removed the whole curse from us and had mercy on us with great mercy.
And he blessed us with a great blessing by bringing his hand upon us with gentleness and compassion, refining us for purification, as it is written:
‘I will bring my hand upon you and refine you to purify you.’”
And again, he has removed wicked people from among us,
and people more sinful than anyone else, as it is written: “But I will destroy the disobedient,
and I will remove all the lawless and all the arrogant from among you, and I will appoint your judges as before,
and your counselors as at the beginning.” And they will say, “This is what God has done for us, because we are his servants.”
And the Lord has disciplined us mercifully and corrected us compassionately, because we are his children; he is our Father.
And those who pay attention, or will pay attention, now or at that time, to all the words written in this book will answer and say,
“Cursed is whoever says, ‘These words—or the curses or blessings that this man pronounces—are empty,’
and that they will not come upon anyone as he says. All these curses will come upon them at that time, or indeed now.”
And they will say, “But those who do not believe that the Lord has done all these things for us are dead
and are strangers to the one who created them.”
As it is written, “God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
What, then, does it mean that God is not the God of the dead, but of the living?
So are all those who have died strangers to God? Or do all the living belong to God?
If God is the God of the living alone, and not of the dead, then how could the apostle say,
“None of us will live for himself, and none of us will die for himself.
For if we live, we will live for the Lord; and if we die, we will die for the Lord.
So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
For this is why Christ died and came to life: so that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.”
Therefore, when he says, “God is not the God of the dead, but of the living,” he means that God is not the God of those who are dead in sexual immorality and defilement,
and theft, deceit, false oaths, fighting, contentiousness, envy, hatred, hostility, unbelief, and every evil deed.
And this is what the Lord Jesus meant when he said, “God is not the God of the dead,
but of those who are alive in purity, virginity, virtue, righteousness, truth, and every good deed.”
And those who stand firm in the words of this book, paying attention to them at that time,
or indeed now, will answer and say, “God, God, anyone who hides the words of this book,
or takes offense at any of these words—
may the Lord bring upon them every curse written in all the Scriptures and written in this book, while they are on the earth.”
And the Lord binds the fury of his anger upon them on the day of wrath and throws them into the fiery furnace blazing with a great fire.
According to the Scriptures, people who are not asleep will quickly hear those who call them.
And those who are asleep, too, will rise from sleep if you repeatedly cry out to them.
But dead people, hidden beneath the earth or laid out in the tombs, will not hear if someone calls to them loudly with many words.
Indeed, they will barely become aware at the last trumpet, on the day when the trumpet will sound and the dead will rise imperishable.
This is also how it is with people who are alert in their earnestness through awareness
and love of God: they will quickly hear the holy words of our Lord Jesus through those who teach them in the fear of the Lord.
And those who are held to a small degree by forgetfulness and closed-mindedness—
these others, too, if those who guide them teach them once or twice from the Scriptures, will withdraw.
